 Sen. Susan Collins is responding to calls for more funding for winter heating relief this year while also defending her record.
 Last week, Maine's two representatives called on Congress to give Maine's Low-Income Heat and Energy Assistance Program (LIHEAP) more money.
 Also read: Maine representatives call on Congress for more LIHEAP money 
 They said while heating costs have soared, the financial help hasn't kept pace.
 Representative Jared Golden said: 
 "While Maine’s home heating prices have risen by 80% year to year, LIHEAP’s funding has increased by less than one percent. With winter on the horizon, I’m urging Congress to plug the gap as soon as possible so that Mainers don’t have to face the cold alone.” Heating oil truck in Maine (WGME) 
 Congresswoman Chellie Pingree said:
 “This is a crisis. Whether or not you can heat your home this winter should not be a partisan issue.” Collins says the Appropriations Committee, which she chairs, will consider increasing LIHEAP funding again this year.
 Also read: Maine families feel pressure as heating oil costs continue to rise 
 In a statement, Collins' office declared:
 "Sen. Collins has always been a champion of the LIHEAP program – she increased its funding last year in the appropriations process and called for and secured the early release of this funding last week." She went on to say that she and Sen. Angus King have also called for the release of oil from the Northeast Reserve.
